reasoning.pain_intensity: The evidence describes manual forwarding and device sharing (SIG-001, SIG-004), which is an annoyance but not severe. No mention of lost customers or revenue. Score 2 (mild annoyance).
reasoning.frequency: Forum posts imply recurring need, but no explicit frequency. For a small business with multiple inquiries, it could be daily, but evidence is anecdotal. Score 3 (weekly occurrence).
reasoning.urgency: Workarounds exist (manual forwarding, shared QR code), so the problem is not blocking operations. Score 2 (nice to have).
reasoning.economic_impact: No evidence of dollar cost. No mention of lost sales or compliance fines. Score 1 (negligible).
reasoning.operational_impact: Team coordination is required, but not entire team blocked. Score 2 (minor disruption).
reasoning.workaround_intensity: Manual forwarding and taking turns require some effort but not a full-time role. Score 2 (moderate effort).
reasoning.willingness_to_pay: No evidence that users are paying for solutions. Existing free workarounds are used. Score 1 (no spend).
reasoning.global_applicability: WhatsApp is global, but the specific multi-agent problem may vary by region and WhatsApp Business API availability. Score 3 (moderate applicability).
reasoning.customer_accessibility: Target users are small business owners on Reddit and Shopify forums, reachable but not a clear concentrated channel. Score 3 (some channels).
reasoning.evidence_quality: Only 3 forum posts from 2 independent sources (Reddit, Shopify). No interviews, surveys, or quantitative data. Score 2 (weak).

verified_facts: Users manually forward WhatsApp messages between team members because only one device can be logged into WhatsApp Business at a time (SIG-001).
Users share a single WhatsApp Business number by logging in/out of the same device or using unofficial workarounds (SIG-004).
Users handle customer support inquiries through WhatsApp alongside Shopify Inbox, manually switching between apps (SIG-008).
inferences: The problem occurs for small businesses with multiple support staff who need to share a single WhatsApp Business number.
The current workarounds are time-consuming and may lead to missed messages or inconsistent customer history.
Users are not using the official WhatsApp Business API (which supports multi-agent) likely due to cost, complexity, or lack of awareness.
assumptions: The frequency of the problem is at least weekly for affected users.
Users have not tried or cannot afford paid multi-agent solutions like WhatsApp Business API or third-party tools.
The pain is consistent across different small business verticals.
unknowns: Actual frequency of the problem (daily vs. weekly).
Economic impact (lost revenue, customer churn) – not quantified.
Willingness to pay for a solution – no evidence of spending.
Whether existing solutions (WhatsApp Business API, WATI, etc.) adequately address the need.
overall_assessment: The pain of managing WhatsApp conversations across a team is real but mild. The evidence is limited to three forum posts from two sources, all anecdotal. No economic or operational severity is demonstrated. Users have workarounds that, while inconvenient, are free and functional. Existing paid solutions (WhatsApp Business API, third-party platforms) already address this need, suggesting the market may be saturated or the problem not severe enough to justify a new SaaS product. The opportunity does not meet the threshold of a burning need.
